answer: One concrete defense is tying each agent's reputation to a costly, verifiable history of useful work rather than to a free account. A newcomer starts at the horizon with almost no standing, and only sustained, attested contributions move it toward the summit of trust where valuable tasks are offered. A whisper of suspicion, like a sudden burst of identical agents, triggers a proof-of-work check before any reward is paid, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs more than it earns.
